claim: Bqt4 does not uniformly distribute around the nuclear envelope but rather appears in puncta.
source: Consistent with previously described electron microscopy images (Chikashige et al., 2009), we observe that Bqt4 does not uniformly distribute around the NE but rather appears in puncta, indicating spatial heterogeneity in NE composition (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy observations presented in the manuscript and cited electron microscopy images from Chikashige et al., 2009.

claim: Bqt4 and Man1 signals occasionally overlap but more often do not.
source: Bqt4 and Man1 signals occasionally overlap but more often, they do not (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Domain partitioning is seen when simultaneously viewing Bqt4 and Lem2.
source: Domain partitioning is also seen when simultaneously viewing Bqt4 and Lem2 (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The ring of Lem2 is diminished to near-invisibility in cells lacking Bqt4.
source: Remarkably, the ring of Lem2 is diminished to near-invisibility in cells lacking Bqt4, while a single Lem2 focus remains (Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 2A), colocalizing with the SPB component Pcp1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A) (Gonzalez et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 2A, and cited work from Gonzalez et al., 2012.

claim: Bqt4 is specifically required for distribution of Lem2 around the nuclear envelope.
source: Hence, Bqt4 is specifically required for distribution of Lem2 around the NE.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that Lem2 distribution is lost in bqt4Δ cells but not in other mutants, and that other NE proteins are unaffected by Bqt4 loss.

claim: Bqt4-GFP signal recovers within approximately 12 seconds after photobleaching with a half-life of 5.029 seconds.
source: Bqt4-GFP signal inside the photobleached window recovers within ~12 s (Figure 2B; half-life 5.029 s).
evidence: The claim is supported by FRAP experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The reappearance of Bqt4-GFP signal within the region of interest shows a distinct recovery pattern, appearing progressively from the flanking nuclear envelope edges to the center of the bleached region.
source: Moreover, the reappearance of Bqt4-GFP signal within the ROI consistently shows a distinct recovery pattern; rather than uniformly recovering throughout the bleached NE segment, the signal appears progressively from the flanking NE edges to the center of the bleached region (Figure 2A), suggesting that dissociated Bqt4-GFP is replenished by movement around the NE.
evidence: The claim is supported by FRAP experimental data and observations shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The half life of Lem2 residency beneath the SPB remains unaffected upon Bqt4 loss.
source: At this site, the half life of Lem2 residency remains unaffected upon Bqt4 loss (Figure 2C; Half life, wt: 23.11 s, bqt4∆: 23.99 s).
evidence: The claim is supported by FRAP experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The two distinct pools of Lem2, beneath the SPB and around the nuclear envelope, are controlled by different mechanisms.
source: Hence, the two distinct pools of Lem2, beneath the SPB and around the NE, are controlled by different mechanisms, with Bqt4 controlling the pool of Lem2 that is distributed away from the SPB region around the NE.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the differential effects of Bqt4 loss on the two Lem2 pools.

claim: Csi1 either recruits or stabilizes Lem2 beneath the SPB.
source: Therefore, Csi1 either recruits or stabilizes Lem2 beneath the SPB.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that Lem2 localization beneath the SPB is abolished in csi1Δ cells.

claim: In cells lacking both Bqt4 and Csi1, Lem2-GFP is greatly diminished from the ring around the nuclear envelope but still strongly detectable beneath the SPB.
source: In cells lacking both Bqt4 and Csi1, Lem2-GFP is greatly diminished from the ring around the NE but still strongly detectable beneath the SPB (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The Lem2 turnover rate is substantially increased in csi1∆ bqt4∆ cells relative to wt or bqt4∆ cells.
source: However, FRAP analysis reveals that the Lem2 turnover rate is substantially increased in csi1∆ bqt4∆ cells relative to wt or bqt4∆ cells (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by FRAP experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Csi1 is required to stabilize Lem2 at the LINC region beneath the SPB.
source: Hence, while the initial Lem2 recruitment to the LINC region beneath the SPB is controlled independently of Bqt4 and Csi1, Csi1 is required to stabilize Lem2 at this region; this stabilization is required to counterbalance the Bqt4-dependent mobilization of Lem2 away from the LINC region.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the FRAP data showing increased Lem2 turnover in csi1Δ bqt4Δ cells.

claim: Telomeres have a higher propensity to localize to Bqt4-rich than Man1- or Lem2-rich nuclear envelope domains.
source: Therefore, telomeres have a higher propensity to localize to Bqt4-rich than Man1- or Lem2-rich NE domains.
evidence: The claim is inferred from colocalization data shown in Figure 3D-G and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The intense focus of Lem2 is detectable beneath the SPB.
source: The intense focus of Lem2 detectable in this region (Figure 4A) is consistent with ChIP experiments showing an interaction between Lem2 and centromeres (Barrales et al., 2016; Tange et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 4A and cited ChIP experiments from Barrales et al., 2016 and Tange et al., 2016.

claim: Mis6 sequesters within a Lem2-enriched domain beneath the SPB.
source: Consistent with previous observations (Hiraoka et al., 2011), Mis6 sequesters within a Lem2-enriched domain beneath the SPB (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1, and cited work from Hiraoka et al., 2011.

claim: The central core region and imr localize exclusively to the SPB region, while the pericentric otr sequences associate with nuclear envelope regions away from the SPB.
source: Hence, the central core region and imr localize exclusively to the SPB region, while the pericentric otr sequences associate with NE regions away from the SPB.
evidence: The claim is inferred from microscopy data showing differential localization of centromeric regions relative to the SPB.

claim: Heterochromatin is not required for telomere tethering to the nuclear envelope.
source: However, H3K9me-containing heterochromatin is dispensable for telomeric tethering to the NE, as Tel1L is not dislodged from the NE in clr4Δ cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Tel1L localizes to the nuclear periphery in 80% of wt settings whether early/mid S-phase or late S/G2.
source: In 80% of wt settings, Tel1L localizes to the nuclear periphery (Figure 4C) whether early/mid S-phase or late S/G2.
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The role of Bqt4 in localizing telomeres to the nuclear envelope is more pronounced during late S/G2 than in early S phase.
source: Hence, the role of Bqt4 in localizing telomeres to the NE is more pronounced during late S/G2 than in early S phase.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that Tel1L dislodgement in bqt4Δ cells is more substantial in late S/G2 phase than in early/mid-S phase.

claim: Tel1L remains at the periphery throughout the cell cycle in lem2Δ cells.
source: In contrast to bqt4Δ cells, Tel1L remains at the periphery throughout the cell cycle in lem2Δ cells (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Loss of tethering in a bqt4Δ setting is not a function of losing Lem2 from telomeric tethering sites.
source: Hence, loss of tethering in a bqt4Δ setting is not a function of losing Lem2 from telomeric tethering sites.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that Tel1L remains at the periphery in lem2Δ cells.

claim: Taz1 localizes strongly to the periphery and is delocalized only during late S/G2 in the absence of Bqt4.
source: Taz1 localizes strongly to the periphery and is delocalized only during late S/G2 in the absence of Bqt4 (Figure 4D).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The mat locus is dislodged from the nuclear envelope in early/mid-S phase in bqt4Δ cells.
source: While peripheral localization was observed during both S and G2-phase in wt cells, mat is dislodged from the NE in early/mid-S phase in bqt4Δ cells (Figure 4D).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The mat locus re-localizes to the nuclear envelope in late S/G2 in bqt4Δ cells.
source: This dislodgment is transient, as mat re-localizes to the NE in late S/G2.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the microscopy data showing mat localization patterns in bqt4Δ cells.

claim: The mat locus replicates in early S phase, while telomeres replicate in late S phase.
source: The mat locus replicates in early S phase, while telomeres replicate in late S phase (Hayano et al., 2012; Hayashi et al., 2009; Kim et al., 2003).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Hayano et al., 2012; Hayashi et al., 2009; Kim et al., 2003.

claim: Bqt4 is necessary for tethering telomeres and the mat locus specifically while they undergo DNA replication.
source: Hence, we postulated that Bqt4 is necessary for tethering these loci specifically while they undergo DNA replication.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the correlation between replication timing and dislodgment timing in bqt4Δ cells.

claim: In a taz1Δ background, telomeres replicate throughout the cell cycle.
source: To assess this possibility, we abolished the late specificity of telomere replication by deleting the gene encoding Taz1; in a taz1Δ background, telomeres replicate throughout the cell cycle (Dehé et al., 2012; Tazumi et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Dehé et al., 2012 and Tazumi et al., 2012.

claim: In a bqt4∆ taz1∆ background, telomere dislodgement occurs throughout all stages monitored.
source: In contrast, in a bqt4∆ taz1∆ setting in which telomere replication timing is deregulated, telomere dislodgement occurs throughout all stages monitored (Figure 4E).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Swi6 binds heterochromatic DNA at the mat locus and causes early replication by promoting the recruitment of the replication initiation factor Sld3.
source: Swi6 binds heterochromatic DNA at the mat locus, and causes early replication by promoting the recruitment of the replication initiation factor Sld3 (Hayashi et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Hayashi et al., 2009.

claim: In swi6∆ cells, the mat locus remains tethered to the nuclear envelope.
source: In swi6∆ cells, mat remains tethered to the NE (Figure 4F), eliminating the possibility that Swi6 itself may affect tethering.
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: In swi6∆ bqt4∆ cells, the mat locus is dislodged later, during late S/G2 phase.
source: However, in swi6∆ bqt4∆ cells, the mat locus is dislodged later, during late S/G2 phase (Figure 4F).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: One or two replication foci are observed at the nuclear envelope during late S/G2.
source: One or two such replication foci are observed at the NE during late S/G2 (Meister et al., 2007; Natsume et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Meister et al., 2007 and Natsume et al., 2008.

claim: There is significant colocalization between telomeres and replication foci at the nuclear envelope in wt cells.
source: Consistent with published data (Meister et al., 2007), we observe significant colocalization between telomeres and replication foci at the NE in wt cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data and citation to Meister et al., 2007.

claim: In the absence of Bqt4, Taz1 and Polα show colocalization but this colocalization does not occur at the nuclear envelope.
source: In contrast, while Taz1 and Polα show colocalization in the absence of Bqt4, this colocalization does not occur at the NE (Figure 4H), again indicating that the tendency of telomeres to replicate at the periphery requires Bqt4-mediated tethering.
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 4H.

claim: bqt4Δ cells are hypersensitive to both hydroxyurea and methyl methanesulfonate.
source: Bqt4 is required for cellular resistance to agents that induce DNA damage during S-phase, as bqt4Δ cells are hypersensitive to both hydroxyurea (HU) and methyl methanesulfonate (MMS; Figure 5A)
evidence: The claim is supported by viability assay data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Bqt4 is dispensible for resistance to bleomycin.
source: in contrast, Bqt4 is dispensible for resistance to bleomycin, which induces DNA damage independently of DNA replication (Manolis et al., 2001), and to the microtubule destabilizing agent thiabendazole (Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by viability assay data shown in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A, and citation to Manolis et al., 2001.

claim: The nuclear envelope localization of Bqt4 is required for resistance to MMS.
source: GFP-Bqt4-ΔTM confers similar MMS hypersensitivity to that of bqt4+ deletion while GFP-Bqt4 alone does not (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B), indicating that the NE localization of Bqt4 is required for resistance to MMS.
evidence: The claim is supported by viability assay data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: clr4Δ confers synthetic lethality with bqt4Δ on MMS.
source: However, clr4Δ confers synthetic lethality with bqt4Δ on MMS (Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is supported by viability assay data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Bqt4 and Clr4 play separate, redundant roles in controlling MMS resistance.
source: Therefore, Bqt4 and Clr4 play separate, redundant roles in controlling MMS resistance.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the synthetic lethality of bqt4Δ clr4Δ on MMS.

claim: Polα-GFP accumulates around the nuclear envelope in S-phase cells harboring Man1-GBP.
source: In contrast, Polα-GFP accumulates around the NE in S-phase cells harboring Man1-GBP (Figure 6A).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: In nearly all Man1-GBP/Pol α-GFP cells, the Rad11 foci colocalize with peripherally localized Polα-GFP.
source: By contrast, in nearly all Man1-GBP/Pol α-GFP cells, the Rad11 foci colocalize with peripherally localized Polα-GFP (Figure 6—figure supplement 2B), suggesting that the bulk of DNA replication takes place at the Man1 microdomains
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Centromeric heterochromatin maintenance is compromised by inducing centromeres to replicate at Man1 regions, away from the Lem2 microdomains.
source: Hence, centromeric heterochromatin maintenance is compromised by inducing centromeres to replicate at Man1 regions, away from the Lem2 microdomains.
evidence: The claim is inferred from ChIP-Seq data showing reduced H3K9me2 at pericentromeres in Man1-GBP Polα-GFP cells.

claim: In the absence of Bqt4, H3K9me2 levels are increased over the subtelomeric region at the left end of Chr I.
source: In a wt background, the 35 Kb region near the left end of Chr I is enriched with H3K9me2 (Figure 7A). In the absence of Bqt4, H3K9me2 levels are increased over this subtelomeric region (Figure 7A)
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-Seq data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Subtelomere 2L shows increased H3K9me2 enrichment in the bqt4∆ setting.
source: subtelomere 2L also shows increased H3K9me2 enrichment in the bqt4∆ setting (Figure 7B).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-Seq data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: In bqt4Δ cells, the distinct H3K9me2 transition zone at the boundary between telomeric heterochromatin and the euchromatic chromosome arm is not observed.
source: Moreover, while a sharp decrease in H3K9me2 enrichment is noticeable at the boundary between telomeric heterochromatin and the euchromatic chromosome arm in wt cells, this distinct H3K9me2 transition zone is not observed in bqt4Δ cells, in which additional H3K9me2 peaks extend into adjacent, normally euchromatic, regions.
evidence: The claim is inferred from ChIP-Seq data comparing wt and bqt4Δ cells.

claim: Non-telomeric heterochromatic regions, such as that surrounding the mei4 gene, show normal H3K9me2 profiles in the absence of Bqt4.
source: However, non-telomeric heterochromatic regions, such as that surrounding the mei4 gene (1.4 Mb from Tel2L) (Zofall et al., 2012), show normal H3K9me2 profiles in the absence of Bqt4 (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-Seq data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B and citation to Zofall et al., 2012.

claim: Pericentric H3K9me2 enrichment is slightly reduced by bqt4+ deletion.
source: In contrast to subtelomeres, pericentric H3K9me2 enrichment is slightly reduced by bqt4+ deletion (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-Seq data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A.

claim: H3K9me2 enrichment at the mat locus is substantially reduced in bqt4Δ cells.
source: and H3K9me2 enrichment at the mat locus is substantially reduced (Figure 7—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-Seq data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Bqt4 is dispensable for subtelomeric silencing.
source: Therefore, Bqt4 is dispensable for subtelomeric silencing, but the extent and robustness of subtelomeric silencing are both limited by the presence of Bqt4.
evidence: The claim is inferred from silencing assay data showing that ura4 is repressed in bqt4Δ cells.

claim: The extent and robustness of subtelomeric silencing are both limited by the presence of Bqt4.
source: Therefore, Bqt4 is dispensable for subtelomeric silencing, but the extent and robustness of subtelomeric silencing are both limited by the presence of Bqt4.
evidence: The claim is inferred from silencing assay data showing enhanced variegation in bqt4Δ cells.

claim: Bqt4 does not appear to regulate silencing at the telomeric regions approximately 500 bp from chromosome end.
source: In contrast to the subtelomeres, Bqt4 does not appear to regulate silencing at the telomeric regions (~500 bp from chromosome end; Figure 7—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by silencing assay data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Telomere replication in Man1-adjacent, rather than Bqt4-adjacent, microdomains leads to mis-regulated H3K9me2 maintenance.
source: Therefore, telomere replication in Man1-adjacent, rather than Bqt4-adjacent, microdomains leads to mis-regulated H3K9me2 maintenance.
evidence: The claim is inferred from ChIP-Seq data in Man1-GBP Polα-GFP cells.

claim: The double deletion lem2Δ dcr1Δ shows markedly reduced viability.
source: Moreover, the double deletion lem2Δ dcr1Δ shows markedly reduced viability, demonstrating that Lem2 acts in a pathway separate from (and redundant with) Dicer-mediated pathways to promote viability.
evidence: The claim is supported by viability assay data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Lem2 acts in a pathway separate from and redundant with Dicer-mediated pathways to promote viability.
source: Moreover, the double deletion lem2Δ dcr1Δ shows markedly reduced viability, demonstrating that Lem2 acts in a pathway separate from (and redundant with) Dicer-mediated pathways to promote viability.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the synthetic lethality of lem2Δ dcr1Δ.

claim: Deletion of epe1 confers suppression of the lem2Δ dcr1Δ inviability, but not to the level of an epe1Δ dcr1Δ strain.
source: Accordingly, deletion of epe1 confers suppression of the lem2Δ dcr1Δ inviability, but not to the level of an epe1Δ dcr1Δ strain (Figure 8A).
evidence: The claim is supported by viability assay data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Lem2 functions both in pericentric heterochromatin maintenance and in centromere/kinetochore maintenance.
source: As discussed below, these results, along with our ChIP-seq and localization data, suggest that Lem2 functions both in pericentric heterochromatin maintenance and in centromere/kinetochore maintenance, which when compromised will make Dicer essential (Folco et al., 2008; Klutstein et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is inferred from genetic interaction data and cited work from Folco et al., 2008 and Klutstein et al., 2015.

claim: Cells harboring lem2+ deletion along with a temperature sensitive allele of Cenp-A (cnp1-1) cannot be obtained at any temperature.
source: Consistent with this idea, we find that we cannot obtain cells harboring lem2+ deletion along with a temperature sensitive allele of Cenp-A (cnp1-1) at any temperature (Takahashi et al., 2000).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations and citation to Takahashi et al., 2000.

claim: Overexpression of Ams2 confers limited viability to lem2Δ cnp1-1 cells at permissive temperature.
source: Overexpression of the Cenp-A loading factor Ams2 has been shown to rescue the temperature sensitivity of cnp1-1 (Figure 8B) (Chen et al., 2003), and introduction of overexpressed Ams2 does confer limited (though vastly reduced relative to lem2+) viability to lem2Δ cnp1-1 cells at permissive temperature (32°C, Figure 8B).
evidence: The claim is supported by viability assay data shown in Figure 8B and citation to Chen et al., 2003.

claim: lem2+ deletion abolishes suppression of cnp1-1 temperature sensitivity by overexpressed Ams2.
source: However, lem2+ deletion abolishes suppression of cnp1-1 temperature sensitivity by overexpressed Ams2 (Figure 8B).
evidence: The claim is supported by viability assay data shown in Figure 8B.

claim: bqt4Δ and dcr1Δ are synthetically sick.
source: However, bqt4Δ and dcr1Δ are synthetically sick and bqt4Δ lem2Δ cells are inviable (data not shown) (Tange et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations and citation to Tange et al., 2016.

claim: bqt4Δ lem2Δ cells are inviable.
source: However, bqt4Δ and dcr1Δ are synthetically sick and bqt4Δ lem2Δ cells are inviable (data not shown) (Tange et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations and citation to Tange et al., 2016.

claim: In the absence of Lem2 or Dcr1, Bqt4 becomes crucial for viability.
source: Hence, in the absence of Lem2 or Dcr1, Bqt4 becomes crucial for viability.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the synthetic lethality/sickness of bqt4Δ with lem2Δ or dcr1Δ.

claim: Bqt4 regulates the replication of specific chromosome regions via two separable modes: by tethering specific heterochromatic regions and by mobilizing Lem2 to sites around the nuclear envelope.
source: Bqt4 regulates the replication of specific chromosome regions via two separable modes: First, by tethering specific heterochromatic regions, Bqt4-microdomains promote the fidelity of DNA replication and reassembly of heterochromatin in the wake of the replication fork. Second, Bqt4 mobilizes Lem2 to sites around the NE to promote pericentric heterochromatin maintenance.
evidence: The claim summarizes the main findings of the study.

claim: The subset of Lem2 molecules sequestered beneath the SPB influences CenpA loading and kinetochore maintenance.
source: Our results suggest separable roles for Lem2 as well; the subset of Lem2 molecules sequestered beneath the SPB influences CenpA loading and kinetochore maintenance, while the Bqt4-mobilized subset of Lem2 molecules promotes pericentric heterochromatin maintenance.
evidence: The claim is inferred from genetic interaction data and localization studies.

claim: The Bqt4-mobilized subset of Lem2 molecules promotes pericentric heterochromatin maintenance.
source: Our results suggest separable roles for Lem2 as well; the subset of Lem2 molecules sequestered beneath the SPB influences CenpA loading and kinetochore maintenance, while the Bqt4-mobilized subset of Lem2 molecules promotes pericentric heterochromatin maintenance.
evidence: The claim is inferred from ChIP-Seq data and localization studies.

claim: The central function of Bqt4 is to provide a 'safe zone' within the nucleus in which duplication of difficult-to-replicate repeats, as well as their underlying chromatin, is facilitated.
source: Collectively, our data suggest a model in which the central function of Bqt4 is to provide a 'safe zone' within the nucleus in which duplication of difficult-to-replicate repeats, as well as their underlying chromatin, is facilitated.
evidence: The claim is a model proposed based on the collective data presented in the study.

claim: Bqt4 has been implicated in the interphase positioning of telomeres, which form two to three clusters at the nuclear envelope.
source: Bqt4 has been implicated in the interphase positioning of telomeres, which form two to three clusters at the NE (Funabiki et al., 1993; Chikashige et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Funabiki et al., 1993 and Chikashige et al., 2009.

claim: The relatively high mobility of Bqt4 along the nuclear envelope allows the flexibility to keep contact with telomeres as they unwind and accommodate the replisome.
source: Conceivably, the relatively high mobility of Bqt4 along the NE allows the flexibility to keep contact with telomeres as they unwind and accommodate the replisome.
evidence: The claim is a speculation based on the observed mobility of Bqt4.

claim: Not all loci come under Bqt4 control, as the euchromatic arm locus cut3+ shows neither nuclear envelope enrichment nor Bqt4 dependent localization.
source: Nevertheless, it is clear that not all loci come under such Bqt4 control, as the euchromatic arm locus we studied (cut3+) shows neither NE enrichment nor Bqt4 dependent localization.
evidence: The claim is supported by localization data for cut3+.

claim: The specificity of Bqt4 interaction with non-telomeric loci may be determined via its N-terminal DNA-binding domain.
source: The specificity of Bqt4 interaction with non-telomeric loci may be determined via its N-terminal DNA-binding domain, which shows homology to a family of fungal transcription factors; alternatively, by analogy with the telomeric Taz1-Rap1-Bqt4 interaction, Bqt4 may contact mat via other DNA binding proteins.
evidence: The claim is a speculation about the mechanism of Bqt4 specificity.

claim: Bqt4-microdomains are important for cellular resistance to agents that cause DNA damage during replication.
source: Bqt4-microdomains are important for cellular resistance to agents that cause DNA damage during replication.
evidence: The claim is supported by viability assay data showing hypersensitivity of bqt4Δ cells to HU and MMS.

claim: The sensitivity of bqt4Δ cells to DNA damaging agents stems from damage specifically to the chromatin regions that are tethered by Bqt4 to the nuclear envelope.
source: We propose a model in which this sensitivity stems from damage specifically to the chromatin regions (eg, telomeres) that are tethered by Bqt4 to the NE.
evidence: The claim is a model proposed based on the observed hypersensitivity of bqt4Δ cells.

claim: Repetitive regions are particularly challenging for the replication machinery.
source: Indeed, these repetitive regions are particularly challenging for the replication machinery (Miller et al., 2006), and HU or MMS likely exacerbate the level of stalled and/or collapsed forks in these regions.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Miller et al., 2006.

claim: Bqt4-rich domains are specialized microenvironments in which collisions between replication and transcription machineries are robustly handled or avoided.
source: In particular, we suggest that Bqt4-rich domains are specialized microenvironments in which collisions between replication and transcription machineries are robustly handled or avoided.
evidence: The claim is a model proposed based on the genetic interaction data.

claim: When H3K9me-containing heterochromatin is abolished, the resulting transcriptional increase heightens the danger of collisions with the replisome, in turn heightening the need for Bqt4-mediated tethering.
source: The synthetic lethality of bqt4+ and clr4+ on MMS suggests that when H3K9me-containing heterochromatin is abolished, the resulting transcriptional increase heightens the danger of collisions with the replisome, in turn heightening the need for Bqt4-mediated tethering.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the synthetic lethality of bqt4Δ clr4Δ on MMS.

claim: Bqt4 becomes crucial for viability in unperturbed conditions when Dicer is missing.
source: Consistently, Bqt4 becomes crucial for viability even in unperturbed conditions when Dicer, which has been shown to promote transcriptional termination at sites of replication stress via eviction of RNAP2, is missing.
evidence: The claim is supported by the synthetic sickness of bqt4Δ dcr1Δ.

claim: Bqt4 becomes important in HAATI cells, in which rDNA repeats form all chromosomal termini.
source: The notion that Bqt4-microdomains are 'safe zones' for replication of repetitive regions can explain our initial observation that Bqt4 becomes important in HAATI cells, in which rDNA repeats form all chromosomal termini, leading cells to harbor on average six-fold more rDNA than wt cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by the initial observation that led to the study.

claim: Bqt4-rich regions may exclude RNAP2 or concentrate the Pif1 helicase.
source: These regions may exclude RNAP2 or concentrate the Pif1 helicase, which allows replication to negotiate the transcription machinery (Sabouri et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is a speculation about the mechanism of Bqt4-rich regions, with citation to Sabouri et al., 2012.

claim: The accumulation of telomeric transcripts (TERRA) is reduced specifically during telomere replication.
source: The accumulation of telomeric transcripts (TERRA) is reduced specifically during telomere replication (Azzalin and Lingner, 2015); conceivably, this reduction depends on localization to the Bqt4-rich domain.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Azzalin and Lingner, 2015.

claim: The reduction in TERRA accumulation during telomere replication may depend on localization to the Bqt4-rich domain.
source: The accumulation of telomeric transcripts (TERRA) is reduced specifically during telomere replication (Azzalin and Lingner, 2015); conceivably, this reduction depends on localization to the Bqt4-rich domain.
evidence: The claim is a speculation based on the known reduction in TERRA during telomere replication.

claim: The effect of Bqt4 on pericentric heterochromatin maintenance likely stems from loss of Lem2 from SPB-distal sites.
source: Hence, the effect of Bqt4 on pericentric heterochromatin maintenance likely stems from loss of Lem2 from these SPB-distal sites.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the localization data showing distinct localization patterns for centromere cores and pericentric regions.

claim: Compromised Cnp1 maintenance would necessitate robust pericentric heterochromatin, which is required for establishment of Cnp1 at centromere sequences.
source: Compromised Cnp1 maintenance would necessitate robust pericentric heterochromatin, which is required for establishment of Cnp1 at centromere sequences (Folco et al., 2008); this establishment function is likely compromised when the replication 'safe zone' conferred by Bqt4 is lost.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the genetic interaction data and cited work from Folco et al., 2008.

claim: The potential for replication/transcription collision is severe at pericentromeres.
source: The potential for replication/transcription collision is severe at pericentromeres, where RNAi-mediated release of RNAP2 is required to prevent stalled forks and thereby promote heterochromatin inheritance (Kloc et al., 2008; Zaratiegui et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Kloc et al., 2008 and Zaratiegui et al., 2011.

claim: In a lem2Δ dcr1Δ double mutant, a 'perfect storm' of factors severely confounds viability.
source: Hence, we propose that in a lem2Δ dcr1Δ double mutant, a 'perfect storm' of factors severely confounds viability; Cnp1 maintenance is compromised, replication of the region is highly problematic, and pericentric heterochromatin is abolished, disallowing both kinetochore establishment and kinetochore maintenance.
evidence: The claim is a model proposed to explain the synthetic lethality of lem2Δ dcr1Δ.

claim: Similar replication challenges may alter heterochromatin reassembly at bqt4Δ subtelomeres.
source: Such considerations may also underlie the complete inviability of lem2Δbqt4Δ cells (data not shown) (Tange et al., 2016). Similar replication challenges may alter heterochromatin reassembly at bqt4Δ subtelomeres
evidence: The claim is a speculation about the mechanism underlying altered heterochromatin at bqt4Δ subtelomeres.

claim: Compromised pericentric heterochromatin may contribute to the increased H3K9me2 levels at bqt4Δ subtelomeres by releasing limiting heterochromatin factors.
source: furthermore, by releasing limiting heterochromatin factors, compromised pericentric heterochromatin may contribute to the increased H3K9me2 levels at bqt4Δ subtelomeres (Tadeo et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is a speculation with citation to Tadeo et al., 2013.

claim: The effects of bqt4+ deletion on pericentric and subtelomeric H3K9me2 levels are subtle.
source: We note that the effects of bqt4+ deletion on pericentric and subtelomeric H3K9me2 levels are subtle.
evidence: The claim is an observation from the ChIP-Seq data.

claim: Bqt4 loss fails to confer appreciable sensitivity to the microtubule depolymerizing agent thiabendazole.
source: Likewise, Bqt4 loss fails to confer appreciable sensitivity to the microtubule depolymerizing agent thiabendazole (TBZ, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A) in contrast with Dcr1 loss, which confers TBZ hypersensitivity due to loss of pericentric heterochromatin (Provost et al., 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by viability assay data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and citation to Provost et al., 2002.

claim: Pericentric heterochromatin levels are high enough in bqt4Δ cells to prevent pericentric cohesin levels from dropping beneath the critical threshold that governs TBZ sensitivity.
source: Hence, while pericentric heterochromatin levels are reduced by loss of Bqt4, they are high enough to prevent pericentric cohesin levels from dropping beneath the critical threshold that governs TBZ sensitivity.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the lack of TBZ sensitivity in bqt4Δ cells.

claim: The orderly formation of nuclear microenvironments is even more critical in mammalian genomes with their higher proportion of repetitive sequences and diverse range of chromatin types.
source: The orderly formation of nuclear microenvironments is even more critical in mammalian genomes with their higher proportion of repetitive sequences and diverse range of chromatin types found along the length of a chromosome (Akhtar et al., 2013; Gerhardt et al., 2016; Simonis et al., 2006; Zullo et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is a speculation with citations to Akhtar et al., 2013; Gerhardt et al., 2016; Simonis et al., 2006; Zullo et al., 2012.

claim: The presence of distinct nuclear subdomains may coordinate the fidelity of replication of each chromatin subtype, ensuring that entire chromosomes are inherited with both genetic and epigenetic information intact.
source: For difficult-to-replicate chromatin regions, the presence of distinct nuclear subdomains, with specific molecular compositions tailored to interactions with distinct chromatin subtypes, may coordinate the fidelity of replication of each subtype, ensuring that entire chromosomes are inherited with both genetic and epigenetic information intact.
evidence: The claim is a speculation about the broader implications of the findings.
